label: Databricks

script.preamble:
table.insert(package.searchers,
    function (module_name)
        local loader = package.preload[module_name]
        if(loader == nil) then
            error("Module " .. module_name .. " not found in package.preload.")
        else
            return loader
        end
    end
)

failures.pattern: Invalid access token|HTTP request failed by code: 40[13]
Connection failure while using the OSS Databricks JDBC driver

auth.hint: Create a new personal access token in the workspace (User settings > Developer), then: exakit source reauth {name|lower}

pin_mismatch.message: The certificate of {host} no longer matches the one the kit pinned.
pin_mismatch.hint: Databricks renews its certificates now and then. A check reads the new one, verifies it from this PC and pins it: exakit source check {name|lower}

no_tables.message: Databricks lists no tables in {catalog}.{schema} for this token.
no_tables.hint: The adapter reads tables through the Unity Catalog API, which shows nothing for the shared samples catalog or for a schema the token cannot browse. Use a schema of your own (e.g. workspace.default with a table in it): set EXAKIT_VS_CATALOG and EXAKIT_VS_SCHEMA and run exakit connect databricks again.

import_failed.message: Exasol Personal's import process failed while the Databricks driver connected.
import_failed.hint: The rows travel through the import process and the Databricks JDBC driver (AllowSelfSignedCerts=1, as the import process has no Java trust store). Check that the SQL warehouse is running or can start, then: exakit source check {name|lower}

notes: The adapter's metadata calls are checked against the workspace certificate's SHA-256, pinned when you connect (the certificate is verified from this PC first); rows travel encrypted through the JDBC driver.
Upstream limits: at most 50 tables per virtual schema, BINARY columns are not supported, and TABLE_FILTER is not available.
